cards.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Open Foundation Model Hits #1 on Four Tabular Benchmarks
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on enterprise ML pipelines, a zero-shot tabular model that tops TabArena, BeyondArena, TALENT, and ScoringBench without training or feature engineering is a direct alternative to the XGBoost/LightGBM workflow.
cards.summary: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular is an open foundation model (28M–215M params) for tabular classification and regression. It performs in-context learning in a single forward pass with no fine-tuning, using column, row, and in-context attention (column attention scales linearly with rows). Pretrained on synthetic data only; released under OpenMDW-1.1 for commercial use on Hugging Face.

cards.title: ProvenanceGuard: Source-Aware Factuality Verification for MCP-Based LLM Agents
cards.why_it_matters: As LLM agents increasingly route over multiple tools, cross-source conflation is a silent failure mode; this post-generation verification layer is directly applicable to any multi-source agent pipeline you might build.
cards.summary: ProvenanceGuard is a post-generation verification layer for MCP agents that tracks source identity through the full pipeline rather than pooling evidence. It decomposes answers into claims, routes each to its most relevant source, checks NLI support (DeBERTa), verifies attribution match, and emits per-claim and answer-level verdicts. Blocked answers go through RARR-style repair and re-verification.

cards.title: Skill-Space Shooting: Foundation-Model-Guided Policy Improvement Without Human Demos
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers working on robot learning and autonomous agents, this proposes a scalable correction mechanism that bypasses per-task human demonstration by leveraging reusable skill primitives.
cards.summary: Skill-space shooting uses foundation model guidance to search for corrective behaviors—short, reusable skills—and converts successful trials into policy improvement signal. Real-world experiments show iterative policy gains without human demonstration, and skills transfer across tasks to reduce the cost of teaching new ones.

cards.title: Imagine3D-LLM: MLLMs Decode Compact 3D Gaussian Representations to Improve Spatial Reasoning
cards.why_it_matters: Teaching MLLMs to internally reconstruct a scene before answering is a novel architectural approach to 3D understanding that could inform how you design multimodal reasoning systems.
cards.summary: Imagine3D-LLM appends learnable summary tokens after image tokens and decodes them into a compact 3D Gaussian Splatting representation supervised by a photometric reconstruction loss, trained jointly with next-token prediction. The reconstruction objective also strengthens cross-frame correspondence in the underlying image features. The model outperforms prior methods across multiple spatial reasoning and 3D understanding benchmarks.

cards.title: STEPQuant: Spatial-Temporal PTQ for Delta-Rule Recurrent States Hits 5x Compression at 6-Bit
cards.why_it_matters: Linear attention models are increasingly viable for long-context serving, and quantizing their recurrent states is the key memory bottleneck this directly addresses with concrete gains on Qwen3 and Kimi-Linear.
cards.summary: STEPQuant is a post-training quantization framework for Delta-rule recurrent states that allocates precision by error magnitude and memory lifetime, jointly fitting key-row and value-column scales. On Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct, 6-bit STEPQuant matches FP32 accuracy and outperforms uniform INT8 at 4-bit. Integrated into SGLang, it achieves over 5x recurrent-state compression and reduces total serving memory by up to 68.7%.

cards.title: Theory Paper: Semantic Speciation and Nonlocality Windows in Generative Models Proven to Coincide
cards.why_it_matters: If you study diffusion or autoregressive dynamics, this theoretical result formally links two empirically observed phenomena—semantic class commitment and long-range dependency onset—under a common-cause hypothesis.
cards.summary: The paper formalizes two temporal windows in generative model dynamics: a speciation window (when a sample commits to a semantic class) and a nonlocality window (when local context becomes insufficient). Under a 'common cause' hypothesis—that semantic labels explain a fraction of long-range token correlations—the authors prove the nonlocality window must lie within the speciation window. Both windows shrink to a single phase transition as system size grows, verified analytically in Gaussian mixtures.
